claims.explanation: Isoxsuprine is a beta-adrenergic agonist that also inhibits CDK1, and its selective killing likely depends on CDK1 dependency and intact beta-adrenergic signaling. TP53 mutation is common in sensitive lines but also in resistant lines, so it is not sufficient; instead, sensitivity may be driven by high CDK1 expression or loss of protective pathways such as PTEN, while resistance may be mediated by NF1 mutations or other alterations that reduce CDK1 reliance.

features.basis: Isoxsuprine inhibits CDK1 (PMID 20638755); high CDK1 expression may predict sensitivity.
Isoxsuprine is an ADRB2 agonist; high receptor expression may enhance downstream effects.
TP53 mutations are frequent in sensitive lines, possibly due to impaired DNA damage response.
PTEN loss may increase dependence on CDK1 or beta-adrenergic signaling.
NF1 mutations appear enriched in resistant lines, possibly via RAS pathway activation.
BRAF mutations are common in resistant melanoma lines, suggesting MAPK-driven resistance.
KRAS mutations appear in several resistant lines, possibly reducing CDK1 dependence.
EGFR mutations are present in some sensitive lung lines, but mechanism unclear.
PIK3CA mutations are seen in several sensitive lines, possibly altering survival signaling.
CDKN2A loss may increase CDK1 activity and sensitivity to CDK1 inhibition.
